On shady slopes above around 2500 m the snowpack is in places cohesive. Where terrain roughness is already smoothed out on smooth ground, avalanches can in some places be triggered in the old snow.

CH.coreZoneText: Danger level "moderate" (2-) in northwest to northeast to east facing aspects above 2600m.

avalancheProblems.comment:
As a consequence of a sometimes strong westerly wind, wind slabs will form. They will be deposited on a weakly bonded old snowpack in particular on steep shady slopes above approximately 2600 m. The fresh wind slabs are mostly small but can in some cases be released easily. The avalanche prone locations are to be found in particular in gullies and bowls.
Backcountry touring calls for careful route selection. The Avalanche Warning Service currently has only a small amount of information that has been collected in the field, so that the avalanche danger should be investigated especially thoroughly in the relevant locality.
